newsitem.title: USA: Carol Foreman seeks top US meat safety job - sources.
newsitem.headline: Carol Foreman seeks top US meat safety job - sources.

text.p: Consumer activist Carol Tucker Foreman has mounted a campaign to be named undersecretary for food safety at the U.S. Agriculture Department, meat industry sources said Monday.
Foreman held a similar post under President Carter.

Producer groups and some meatpackers said they opposed her bid for the top meat inspection and food safety job at USDA, saying she sensationalized risks of meat-borne illness in recent years as the U.S. meat inspection system was being modernized. The first part of the new system, which will test for disease-causing pathogens, takes effect this month.
However, Foreman, who heads a coalition of labor unions and consumer groups who favor meat inspection reform, could expect support from consumer groups.

The food safety post is one of four undersecretary portfolios becoming vacant with President Clinton's second term. The others oversee public-feeding programs, agricultural research, and farm-subsidy and export promotion programs.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said last week that he hoped to begin filling the vacancies by the end of January.
Lobbyists from cattle and pork producer groups said they planned to argue to Glickman against appointment of Foreman.
